---
title: "Factorization"
---

Moran and McCloy's [PHOIBLE 2.0 release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.2593234) collects phonological inventory records contributed by many descriptive sources. The PHOIBLE [download page](https://phoible.org/download) says CC BY-SA 3.0, while the metadata for the exact Zenodo archive lists CC BY 3.0 and the archive contains no separate license file. The course copy follows the CC BY 3.0 terms attached to that archived release and records the project-page discrepancy here. An inventory record generally describes a doculect, but multiple records may share a Glottocode and some source collections aggregate several varieties. Thus one row in the course matrix is an inventory record selected within a Glottocode, not an unqualified language.

Two earlier ideas organize the module. [Variance](../random-variables-and-distributions/variance-and-covariance.qmd) measures squared variation around a mean, while covariance records how two columns vary together; PCA will apply those ideas to segment-listing columns. The [validation split](choosing-components.qmd#separating-fitting-selection-and-evaluation) later chooses a reconstruction rank on held-out inventory records while leaving most cells in each record visible.

The collection proceeds from matrix construction and preprocessing through rank-one structure, SVD, PCA, scores, and loadings, then evaluates reconstruction, rank choice, and a downstream VALEX prediction task.

```{r}
#| label: factorization-index-data

phoible <- readRDS("data/phoible/phoible-pilot.rds")

factorization_inventory <- data.frame(
  object = c(
    "source CLDF value rows",
    "source inventory records",
    "source Glottocodes",
    "retained consonant and vowel memberships",
    "retained segment records"
  ),
  count = c(
    phoible$provenance$original_value_rows,
    phoible$provenance$original_inventories,
    phoible$provenance$original_glottocodes,
    nrow(phoible$memberships),
    nrow(phoible$segments)
  )
)

factorization_inventory
```

Here is a miniature version of the two representations used in this module,
constructed from the prepared course files rather than invented values.

```{r}
index_inventory <- phoible$inventories[1, ]
index_memberships <- phoible$memberships[
  phoible$memberships$inventory_id == index_inventory$inventory_id,
]
listed_ids <- unique(index_memberships$segment_id)
unlisted_id <- setdiff(phoible$segments$segment_id, listed_ids)[1]
index_segment_ids <- c(listed_ids[1:2], unlisted_id)
index_segment_example <- data.frame(
  language = index_inventory$language_name,
  glottocode = index_inventory$glottocode,
  segment = phoible$segments$segment[
    match(index_segment_ids, phoible$segments$segment_id)
  ],
  database_cell = as.integer(index_segment_ids %in% listed_ids)
)

analysis_root <- "data/valex-megaacceptability/audited"
index_valex <- read.csv(
  gzfile(file.path(analysis_root, "valex-counts.csv.gz")),
  check.names = FALSE
)
index_mega <- read.csv(
  gzfile(file.path(analysis_root, "megaacceptability-responses.csv.gz")),
  check.names = FALSE
)
index_verb <- index_mega$verb[[1]]
index_judgments <- index_mega[index_mega$verb == index_verb, ][1:2, ]
index_counts <- unlist(index_valex[index_valex$verb == index_verb, -1])
index_nonzero <- order(index_counts, decreasing = TRUE)[1:2]
index_valex_example <- data.frame(
  verb = index_verb,
  VALEX_frame = names(index_counts)[index_nonzero],
  corpus_count = as.numeric(index_counts[index_nonzero])
)

knitr::kable(index_segment_example)
knitr::kable(index_valex_example)
knitr::kable(index_judgments)
```

The PHOIBLE row has one observed cell for each of three segment columns: one means
that a retained source row lists the segment, while zero means only that no such
row is listed. The VALEX row has one corpus-derived count for each subcategorization
frame. The two MegaAcceptability rows are participant judgments of two experimental
frames for the same verb. Their later verb-by-frame mean is a derived aggregate,
not another raw response. A cell would be unobserved if its value were unavailable
under the data protocol; an observed zero remains a recorded database value.

The prepared memberships exclude tone entries and rows explicitly marked as marginal. A matrix cell equal to one means that a retained PHOIBLE value row links an inventory record to a segment. A zero means that no such row is listed under this preparation; it is not direct evidence that a language lacks the segment.

The first eight pages study a matrix-completion task: whether structure learned from training records helps reconstruct a small set of hidden database cells in a held-out record whose other cells remain visible. The target is database completion under a declared preparation rule, not recovery of a complete phonological system from no observations.

## Constructing and decomposing the matrix

[Linguistic data matrices](data-matrices.qmd) define the row, column, and cell units, reproduce the Glottocode-level row selection, and retain segment columns using training records only. [Centering and scaling](centering-and-scaling.qmd) then compare two transformations of the empirical binary columns. The primary analysis centers without variance standardization because standardization would give relatively greater weight to rare listings.

[Rank-one structure](rank-one-structure.qmd) fits the first singular triplet and places the observed centered cells beside their rank-one reconstruction. [Singular value decomposition](singular-value-decomposition.qmd) extends that fit to ordered orthogonal terms. [Principal component analysis](principal-component-analysis.qmd) derives the covariance identity from the same decomposition and adds macroarea only after fitting for descriptive interpretation.

## Interpreting and evaluating components

[Scores and loadings](scores-and-loadings.qmd) distinguish coordinates for inventory rows from directions over segment columns. A loading pattern may suggest a linguistic hypothesis, but the decomposition does not turn a component into a natural class, universal, or causal mechanism.

[Reconstruction](reconstruction.qmd) hides listed and not-listed cells in each held-out record, estimates scores from the remaining cells, and returns predictions to the original cell scale. [Choosing components](choosing-components.qmd) selects rank on validation inventories with balanced reconstruction loss and reserves test inventories for one final comparison. Because families are not the split unit, the result does not establish transfer to unseen language families.

## From decomposition to supervised prediction

The final application changes both the dataset and the target. [VALEX](https://ilexir.co.uk/valex/) contains GPL-licensed, automatically acquired English verb subcategorization counts described by [Korhonen, Krymolowski, and Briscoe (2006)](https://www.cs.brandeis.edu/~marc/misc/proceedings/lrec-2006/pdf/558_pdf.pdf). The official [MegaAcceptability archive](https://megaattitude.io/projects/mega-acceptability/mega-acceptability-v1.zip) is CC BY-SA 4.0; its internal README identifies the release as v1.2. It contains ordinal judgments of English clause-embedding verbs in experimentally controlled frames, and [White and Rawlins (2020)](https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.1001) analyze how corpus distributions relate to those profiles.

The [VALEX--MegaAcceptability page](valex-megaacceptability.qmd) predicts MegaAcceptability profiles from VALEX subcategorization-frame proportions and compares the direct proportions with a PCA-compressed representation for verbs absent during fitting. Participant normalization, response aggregation, predictor centering, PCA, and tuning all occur inside their training splits. The application asks whether this shallow compression helps the held-out-verb target. It does not treat automatically acquired counts as grammatical labels or test abstract linguistic representations in general.

## Module recap and roadmap

1. [Linguistic data matrices](data-matrices.qmd#phoible-measurement-dossier)
   construct the PHOIBLE row, column, and cell units.
2. [Centering and scaling](centering-and-scaling.qmd) fix the origin and weighting
   of those cells.
3. [Rank-one structure](rank-one-structure.qmd) and the
   [SVD](singular-value-decomposition.qmd) decompose the centered matrix.
4. [PCA](principal-component-analysis.qmd) and
   [scores and loadings](scores-and-loadings.qmd) interpret row coordinates and
   column directions.
5. [Reconstruction](reconstruction.qmd) and
   [rank selection](choosing-components.qmd) evaluate hidden PHOIBLE cells.
6. The [VALEX--MegaAcceptability
   application](valex-megaacceptability.qmd#valex-megaacceptability-measurement-dossier)
   validates direct and compressed predictors on held-out verbs.

The sequence thus moves from a declared empirical matrix, through its exact
algebra, to two held-out targets on the original data scales. Begin with the
[PHOIBLE measurement dossier](data-matrices.qmd#phoible-measurement-dossier).
